question: What's new on Raymond James in the last 90 days?

claims.text: Financial Institutions Division expansion (newest, WealthManagement.com, 2026-11-12, trade press, indicative only): Raymond James will add $18.7 billion and 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp. The advisors are expected to transition in May 2027. FID president Stephen Kruchten called it a "significant and highly strategic expansion" of the firm's relationship with Pinnacle Financial Partners.
FID scale (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-23): the trade press describes FID as established in 1987 and says it currently serves about 950 advisors across 160 institutions.

Recruiting, November 2026 (trade press): WealthManagement.com (2026-11-05) reported a three-advisor team that previously managed over $1.5 billion at PNC Private Bank joining to operate as KKM Wealth Partners within Alex. Brown. InvestmentNews (2026-11-05) reported the Mintz & Gow Group, adding more than $1.2 billion from Truist Investment Services to the employee advisor channel in Richmond, Virginia. A piece dated 2026-11-06 noted a $700 million advisor team had joined earlier that week, the second in as many weeks to join the firm managing that amount.

Fiscal fourth-quarter results as reported by trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-29): record quarter-end client assets under administration of $1.87 trillion, up 1% sequentially and 12% year-over-year. Private Client Group net revenue was a record $3.06 billion, up 15% year-over-year, with pre-tax income of $458 million, up 10%. Domestic PCG net new assets rose 88% for the fiscal year to a record of more than $98 billion. Non-GAAP EPS was $3.59 on revenue of $4.74 billion, up 13%.

Advisor headcount and recruiting production: WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) says Raymond James no longer reports advisor headcount, but had about 8,900 advisors the last time it was broken out. InvestmentNews (2026-11-05) cites a record 8,943 advisors at fiscal year-end, up 2% year-over-year. WealthManagement.com (2026-11-05) reports the firm said it recruited $538 million in trailing 12-month production for advisors entering its domestic independent contractor and employee channels during the fiscal year, up from $407 million in the prior year, representing more than $82 billion in client assets.

M&A stance (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-29): when asked about M&A, Shoukry said the firm looks for acquisitions in wealth management in particular, but they would have to be a good cultural and strategic fit. He said, "We don't do acquisitions to slash costs," and that they are done "to grow revenues and to be better firms together over time."

Advisor departures (trade press, indicative only): on 2026-10-27 WealthManagement.com reported a Georgia team with about $1.1 billion, previously with Raymond James Financial Services, going independent and custodying with Fidelity. On 2026-10-16 it reported Janney opening a Houston office seeded by the Edward Fitzpatrick Group, with Raymond James for about 23 years and $3.3 billion in client assets, plus Lance Murphy, who oversaw more than $200 million. On 2026-10-08 it reported four practices with more than $1 billion joining Ascentis Independent Advisors from Raymond James Financial Services. Those practices will continue to use Raymond James as primary custodian. InvestmentNews (2026-08-28) noted that Raymond James had lost two teams to FiNet.

Legal matter (InvestmentNews, 2026-10-19): a FINRA arbitration panel ordered Raymond James & Associates to pay two employee advisors close to $1.86 million in compensatory damages and interest, in a dispute tracing to the 2016 purchase of Deutsche Bank's U.S. private wealth group (the Alex. Brown brand). A Raymond James spokesperson declined to comment.

Product launch, Private Wealth Guided Portfolios (InvestmentNews and WealthManagement.com, 2026-09-29): the firm launched a risk-based model framework combining equity and fixed income with a dedicated alternatives sleeve covering private markets and hedged strategies, aimed at advisors serving high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients. PCG President Tash Elwyn said the firm is "committed to being a destination for private wealth advisors and the clients they serve."

Recruiting, September 2026 (WealthManagement.com and InvestmentNews, 2026-09-24): Raymond James added two teams totaling $1.75B. One was the Iowa-based Greenwood Wealth Partners, with about $1.25 billion from D.M. Kelly & Company, joining the employee channel. The other was Harris Wealth Partners, about $500 million from Commonwealth Financial Network, joining the independent channel in Rochester, N.Y.

Retirement offering (WealthManagement.com, 2026-09-16): per a regulatory filing and a spokesperson, the firm launched a firm-wide SIMPLE IRA Employer Advisory and Consulting Services Program, partnered with Capital Group American Funds. It is designed for small businesses with up to 100 employees and is available to its roughly 8,900 advisors.

Recruiting, August 2026 (InvestmentNews, trade press): on 2026-08-28, David Lazorik joined RJFS as branch manager in Yakima, Washington, from Wells Fargo, where he managed more than $160 million. On 2026-08-21, Adam Pearsall joined Raymond James & Associates from UBS Financial Services, where he managed more than $400 million. An RJFS recruitment was also reported on 2026-08-26.
Recruiting from UBS (InvestmentNews, 2026-11-04): the outlet says an Ohio hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026.

gaps.what: All evidence is trade press (tier 4, indicative only). No primary Raymond James documents, such as the fiscal fourth-quarter earnings release, call transcript, 10-K or press releases, are in the evidence, so the figures above are trade-press reports of firm disclosures.
